newsitem.title: FRANCE: More die in Algeria's "month of all horrors".
newsitem.headline: More die in Algeria's "month of all horrors".

text.p: Moslem rebels have massacred 13 more civilians in Algeria in what the newspaper Liberte on Thursday dubbed "the month of all horrors".
Liberte said the latest reported murders -- a family of six women and five men in one attack and a husband and wife in another -- brought the total number killed to 76 in November
Some civilians, fearing more attacks ahead of a referendum on November 28 to amend the constitution, were reported urging the government to give them arms to protect their communities.

"Arm us! We cannot not defend ourselves with our bare chests," shouted villagers to National Solidarity and Family Minister Rabea Mechernene who visited Ben Salah village where 12 civilians were killed early on Wednesday.

In the latest reported slaughter, Liberte said rebels raided a tiny community near Berrouaghia, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers, overnight Monday. "One family of six women and five men was massacred and several other women were violenty beaten," it said.

El Watan newspaper said Moslem rebels, believed to be members of the feared guerrilla faction "The Falanges of Death", abducted a couple from Oued el Alleug near the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, early on Wednesday.
"The man and his wife had their throats cut and then they were dumped outside (nearby) Boufarik," the paper said.
El Watan said the same guerrilla group which raided Ben Salah also kidnapped and killed the couple from Oued el Alleug.
Liberte said the killers left a message on a bit of carton saying: "It is the fate of anyone who abandons the prayer. Islamic Armed Group. Blood, Blood. Destruction, Destruction".
An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists took a huge lead.
Algerian legal opposition parties put the death toll at 70,000-100,000 while the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front says 120,000 people have died in the five-year-long civil strife.
